description: Saves the result of a train, flight or TfL check to the person’s Untap account, so it appears on their dashboard with its deadline. Accepts the save_claim arguments returned by a check, with the price paid added where the check listed it as missing. The verdict is worked out again from those facts rather than copied. A train journey that is already saved is returned as it is, not saved twice. Requires sign-in to Untap.

category.description: Which kind of check the claim came from.

actual_arrival.description: Optional. Actual arrival as an ISO 8601 datetime, if known.

airline_iata.description: Two-letter IATA airline code, e.g. "BA" for British Airways, "U2" for easyJet.

arrival_iata.description: Three-letter IATA arrival airport code, e.g. "BCN".

booking_reference.description: PNR / airline booking reference if available, otherwise null.

delay_minutes.description: Optional. Arrival delay in minutes, if known.

departure_iata.description: Three-letter IATA departure airport code, e.g. "LHR".

flight_number.description: Flight number including the airline prefix, e.g. "BA2551".

passenger_name.description: Passenger name as printed on the ticket, or null if not visible.

status.description: Optional. What happened to the flight, if known. When left out, Untap looks the flight up in AeroDataBox flight-status records.

flight.description: For category "flight": the flight, in the shape a flight check returns in save_claim.arguments.flight, with ticket_price_pence set.

card_last4.description: Last 4 digits of the contactless card, if shown.

journeys.description: Every journey on the statement. Up to 500 per call.

bus_route.description: Bus route number for bus rows, otherwise null.

end_time.description: Tap-out time as HH:MM, or null.

fare_pence.description: Charge for this row in pence. £2.20 = 220.

from_location.description: Tap-in station / stop name, or null if not shown.

intended_destination.description: Optional, for an incomplete journey with no touch out: the station the person was travelling to. With it, the refund is estimated as the fare charged minus the usual fare to that station. Without it, the figure is an upper limit equal to the whole charge.

is_auto_corrected.description: Optional. True when the statement says TfL has already corrected this journey (for example "Auto-completed" or "Adjusted").

is_daily_cap_hit.description: Optional. True when the statement marks this row as the one where the daily cap was reached.

is_hopper_free.description: Optional. True when the statement shows this fare as a free Hopper fare (a second bus or tram within 60 minutes).

is_incomplete.description: True if this journey has no tap-out recorded (e.g. label "Incomplete" or "No exit").

is_max_fare.description: True if the statement labels this as a max-fare charge for a failed revenue inspection.

is_weekly_cap_hit.description: Optional. True when the statement marks this row as the one where the weekly cap was reached.

mode.description: Transport mode for this row, or "unknown" when the statement does not say.

start_time.description: Tap-in time as HH:MM, or null.

to_location.description: Tap-out station / stop name, or null for incomplete journeys.

tfl.description: For category "tfl": the journeys, in the shape a TfL check returns in save_claim.arguments.tfl.

booking_reference.description: Booking reference if available, otherwise null.

legs.description: Each journey on this booking, in travel order: one for a single, two for a return (outward first), more for a multi-stop booking. Untap works out Delay Repay for each journey and adds them up.

actual_arrival.description: Optional. Actual arrival for this journey as an ISO 8601 datetime, if known. When left out, Untap looks it up.

arrival_station.description: Full arrival station name, e.g. "Edinburgh Waverley".

delay_minutes.description: Optional. Delay at arrival for this journey, in minutes, if known. When left out, Untap looks it up in National Rail records.

departure_station.description: Full departure station name, e.g. "London Kings Cross".

operator_toc_code.description: National Rail two-letter operator code for this journey: VT=Avanti West Coast, CC=c2c, CH=Chiltern Railways, EM=East Midlands Railway, GX=Gatwick Express, GN=Great Northern, GW=Great Western Railway, LE=Greater Anglia, NT=Northern Trains, SW=South Western Railway, SE=Southeastern, SN=Southern, TL=Thameslink, TP=TransPennine Express, AW=Transport for Wales, LM=West Midlands Railway, LN=London Northwestern Railway, XC=CrossCountry, GR=LNER, SR=ScotRail, LD=Lumo, HT=Hull Trains, CS=Caledonian Sleeper

was_cancelled.description: Optional. True when this journey was cancelled. When set, no National Rail lookup is made.

season_type.description: Season tickets only: how long the season runs. The operator divides the season price into single journeys (for example annual 464, monthly 40, weekly 10, flexi 16) and pays a share of one journey. When left out, the result gives the percentage and the method but no amount.

ticket_price_pence.description: Total fare paid in pence for the whole booking. £62.00 = 6200.

ticket_type.description: Ticket type as printed. For "return" and "open_return" the single fare is half the price paid; for "season" the amount is a share of one journey value (see season_type); every other type uses the full price as the single fare.

train.description: For category "train": the train booking, in the shape a train check returns in save_claim.arguments.train, with ticket_price_pence set.

name: save_claim
title: Save a checked claim to your Untap account
